definition: A model compression technique that removes redundant or low-importance weights, neurons, or layers from a trained network.
details: Pruning can significantly reduce model size and inference cost, with structured pruning removing entire neurons/channels and unstructured pruning removing individual weights.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. In plain words: A model compression technique that removes redundant or low-importance weights, neurons, or layers from a trained network. Here is how it actually plays out: Pruning can significantly reduce model size and inference cost, with structured pruning removing entire neurons/channels and unstructured pruning removing individual weights. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Pruning.
